title: Horse series: Lexington, the Blind Hero of Woodburn
summary: Foaled in 1850 at Elisha Warfield's farm, the racehorse Lexington went blind, then led the North American sire list 16 times from Woodburn Stud near Midway.
bodyMarkdown:
[Lexington](https://grokipedia.com/page/Lexington_(horse)) was foaled on March 17, 1850, at The Meadows, the Fayette County farm of Dr. [Elisha Warfield](/people/#elisha-warfield), and was first named Darley. Through Boston, Timoleon, and Sir Archy, he traced back to the imported stallion Diomed, a line that helped shape Bluegrass breeding.

Raced under the name Lexington, he won six of his seven starts. Failing eyesight, which left him nearly blind, ended his racing career.

In 1856 Robert A. Alexander of Woodburn Stud near Midway bought him for $15,000, then a U.S. record price for an American horse. At Woodburn he became known as the "Blind Hero of Woodburn." He led the North American sire list every year from 1861 through 1874, and again after his death, and his offspring helped make the Inner Bluegrass the center of American Thoroughbred breeding.

Lexington died at Woodburn on July 1, 1875.

## Kentucky today

Woodburn is a private working farm in Woodford County, so view it from the public road only. The [Kentucky Association race course](/stories/kentucky-association-1826-lexington-race-course/) story covers the Lexington track where Warfield and other Bluegrass horsemen raced.
